title: Atrophic Vaginitis (Genitourinary Syndrome of Menopause)
hpi_narrative: [Ms] Patient is a [unknown age]-year-old female with [unknown PMH] who presents with Atrophic Vaginitis. Onset is not specified, character and severity are vaginal dryness, discharge and postcoital bleeding. Associated symptoms include vaginal itchiness and pain with intercourse. The clinical question this case forces you to answer is to diagnose the cause of the patient's symptoms and prescribe appropriate treatment.

stacks.label: Physical Exam: General Appearance
stacks.finding: The general examination is extremely useful to determine how sick the patient looks

stacks.label: Physical Exam: Chest / Lungs
stacks.finding: It is important to investigate for lung pathology

stacks.label: Physical Exam: Heart / Cardiovascular
stacks.finding: It is important to investigate for cardiac pathology

stacks.label: Physical Exam: Abdomen
stacks.finding: It is important to investigate for abdominal pathology

stacks.label: Physical Exam: Genitalia
stacks.finding: This is the patient's chief complaint, so this should be examined

stacks.label: CBC with differential
stacks.finding: CBC is always a good screening tool in nearly every patient

stacks.label: Hormone, thyroid stimulating, serum ultrasensitive / Hormone, thyroid stimulating, serum
stacks.finding: A TSH would be a good lab to order to screen for abnormal thyroid levels which could contribute to the patient's current symptoms

stacks.label: Cervical wet mount
stacks.finding: This is to look for infections that could be contributing to the patient's presentation

stacks.finding: This should be prescribed vaginally to help with the vaginal atrophy. Oral has more side effects and could potentially be more dangerous

stacks.label: Vaccine, diphtheria/tetanus/pertussis / Vaccine, diphtheria/tetanus/pertussis/HIB
stacks.finding: Tdap vaccines should be given every 10 years. No history of this was given, so this should be administered

stacks.label: Vaccine, varicella virus
stacks.finding: If a patient is over the age of 50, he should be administered a herpes-zoster immunization. The CDC recommends Shingrix (Recombinant zoster vaccine) as the preferred shingles vaccine and is recommended for healthy adults 50 years and older. Zostavax may still be used to prevent shingles in healthy adults 60 years and older.

stacks.label: Mammography
stacks.finding: All women older than 40 years old should get a yearly clinical breast exam and mammogram (if risk factors are present, start at 35)
